themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a picture next to a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, what the word customer means, what a message is worth. No formula settles these, because the disagreement usually has money or budget attached.
themes.evidence: In the generative content review answers all three models say the real risk is the implied claim, including Gemini's point that a new combination of individually approved claims can still mislead, and the same shape appears in the semantic context layer answers (teams genuinely need different definitions) and in journey orchestration (nobody can price a sale today against fatigue tomorrow).

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key, and the thing being measured often changes while you measure it. So the models start by building a small set of cases they can actually verify, then grade everything else against that.
themes.evidence: Incrementality answers describe platforms that re-optimize against your own test, answer engine answers say there is no stable baseline or click to attribute, identity resolution answers keep proposing a consented panel or a logged-in list as a truth set, and the B2B signal and ad supply answers both say real performance and missing signal look identical in the data.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and force every action through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every agent execution answer across months proposes the same proxy, gateway, or broker with hard spend and audience caps, the consent answers route all data exits through a single checkpoint, and the orchestration answers build one shared contact log that every channel must check before sending.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the one party who holds the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and no one can make them. So the models either try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting and work with what they already own.
themes.evidence: The agentic traffic answers repeat that agents gain by looking human and propose a fast declared-agent lane with better prices, while the orchestration answers say channel owners are paid to keep sending, the ad supply answers say the market profits from unverified volume, and the identity answers say platform owners profit from keeping walls up.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a dollar, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from the outside.
themes.evidence: The consent and deletion answers converge on expiring audience lists, seeded canary profiles, and the admission that a trained model cannot unlearn one person without retraining, and the same opacity drives the incrementality answers about platforms controlling both treatment and evidence, the identity answers about closed platforms, and the agent execution answers about vendors exposing no rollback.
